item.title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring
item.description: arXiv:2611.09465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs. As consequences we obtain a description of any two-step nilpotent variety by generators and relations, an intrinsic characterisation in terms of quadratic term operations, and an account of its abelian core and of the lower central series of its objects in terms of the square ring. Along the way, we associate with any commutative ring $R$ a square ring whose modules, the two-step nilpotent $R$-groups, extend Hall's nilpotent $R$-groups of class two from $2$-binomial rings to arbitrary rings of coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Logan Geenis, Manfred Hartl, Tim Van der Linden

item.title: Reflections of Nichols algebras in braided monoidal categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.08900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\C$ be an essentially small abelian rigid braided monoidal category. We prove a reflection theorem for Nichols algebras in $\Ind(\C)$ and show that tuples admitting all reflections define connected semi-Cartan graphs. As applications, we prove that a finite Nichols algebra has a generating object of length at most one in $PSU(2)_k$ for odd $k\ge3$, in $SU(2)_{4m}$ for $m\ge1$, and in the representation categories of the Virasoro minimal models $\mathcal M(2,p)$ for odd $p\ge5$. In all three families, we prove that every finite pre-Nichols algebra is a Nichols algebra.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Li

item.title: Infinity operad pairs, higher distributivity and spectral Tambara functors
item.description: arXiv:2611.09115v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce an $\infty$-categorical model of operad pairs and their associated bimonoidal categories. We study the related concepts such as cocartesian-cartesian operad pairs, algebra pairs and the Day convolution. Using the Day convolution for operad pairs, we can define distributive functors between a symmetric bimonoidal category and a cartesian closed monoidal category. As an application, we show that for a finite group $G$, the operadic distributive functors from $\mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{Fin}_G)$ to any cartesian closed monoidal category coincides with the distributive functors defined by the distributive diagram. Therefore, we show that the connective $G$-equivariant $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectra are equivalently the spectral $G$-Tambara functors.
item.dc:creator: Aowen Fan

item.title: The center of an associative crossed module
item.description: arXiv:2611.09360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we define a Drinfeld-type center for an associative crossed module and prove that it is canonically the internal category of an explicit crossed module constructed from Mac Lane's bimultiplications. The resulting center carries a canonical multiplicative lifting, which induces a natural strict braiding, establishing its correspondence to a braided crossed module. We also examine the relationship between this center and Huq's categorical center. Finally, we obtain a canonical comparison morphism with Pirashvili's center of Lie crossed modules via the (braided) Liezation functors, which preserves braidings under an injectivity condition.
item.dc:creator: Emzar Khmaladze, Manuel Ladra, David Quiroga, Brais Ramos P\'erez

item.title: How many points does it take to see the homotopy of a space? Minimal acyclic categorical models
item.description: arXiv:2611.09718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every connected homotopy type is the classifying space of a small category, but this general result gives little control over the categories involved. We study finite acyclic categorical models and measure their complexity by the number of objects. Our main tool is the sink lemma, which describes the addition of a sink as the attachment of a cone along an explicit map. Using it, we determine the minimum number of objects required to model spheres, bouquets of spheres, Moore spaces of cyclic groups, real projective spaces, and lens spaces. We also exhibit infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic rigid minimal models of the sphere. To include spaces admitting no finite model, we introduce a truncated invariant measuring the minimum number of objects required for a finite acyclic category to approximate a space through degree n. Spreading a finite monoid over n+1 objects produces such a category with an n-connected map to the monoid's classifying space. For every nontrivial finite group, this bound is optimal, although its classifying space admits no finite acyclic model.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Carcac\'ia-Campos

item.title: Virtual double categories of relations relative to fibrations
item.description: arXiv:2501.17869v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the relationship between virtual double categories and fibrations, or (hyper)doctrines, in the context of categorical logic. We present a construction that produces a virtual double category of relations internal to a fibration with finite products. We characterize the class of fibrations called elementary existential fibrations, a fibrational counterpart of regular logic, as those for which the induced virtual double category is a cartesian equipment. We also show that cartesian equipments arising in this manner are exactly those that satisfy the Frobenius axiom studied by Walters and Wood in the context of cartesian bicategories. Some logical principles, such as the comprehension axiom for predicates and the extensional equality predicate, are characterized as properties of the double categorical structure.
item.dc:creator: Hayato Nasu

item.title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
item.description: arXiv:2610.18302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Mancini

item.title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
item.description: arXiv:2610.38143v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many equivalence relations of mathematics (Green's relations on a semigroup, orbit relations of group actions, ``same value of an invariant'') are defined by allowed transformations, of a morphism on its two sides or of a point of a set. We put them in one framework. A comparison datum produces a category, the comparison category, whose arrows are the allowed transformations, and two morphisms are related when they can be compared in both directions. Its normal form is a Grothendieck construction, so every such relation is mutual reachability for an action; Green's relations, orbit relations and, more generally, relations defined by an invariant are worked out in detail from it. If the way morphisms are transported is an arbitrary function, every relation occurs, so the real constraint is the regularity of the transport. For completely functorial data we show that the relations obtained contain Green's relations and congruences, we study them at two opposite extremes: on finite groups (every morphism invertible) they are described through double cosets, and on nil monoids (only the unit invertible) we prove a collapse theorem. A short plain-language guide to the vocabulary (comparison categories and transport, Grothendieck construction and mutual reachability, functors, pseudofunctors and lax functors, enriched categories, colimits and stabilization) is included for readers who are not specialists.
item.dc:creator: Nizar El Idrissi

item.title: The Yoneda embedding in simplicial type theory
item.description: arXiv:2501.13229v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Riehl and Shulman introduced simplicial type theory (STT), a variant of homotopy type theory which aimed to study not just homotopy theory, but its fusion with category theory: $(\infty,1)$-category theory. While notoriously technical, manipulating $\infty$-categories in simplicial type theory is often easier than working with ordinary categories, with the type theory handling infinite stacks of coherences in the background. We capitalize on recent work by Gratzer et al. defining the $(\infty,1)$-category of $\infty$-groupoids in STT to define presheaf categories within STT and systematically develop their theory. In particular, we construct the Yoneda embedding, prove the universal property of presheaf categories, refine the theory of adjunctions in STT, introduce the theory of Kan extensions, and prove Quillen's Theorem A.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Gratzer, Jonathan Weinberger, Ulrik Buchholtz

item.title: A calculus of types in Isbell nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2606.03369v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify two constructions from different mathematical traditions. In linear logic and realisability, logical types are generated rather than fixed in advance: one begins with a universe of realisers equipped with execution, uses orthogonality to test their interactions, and takes types to be the biorthogonally closed subsets. In enriched Isbell duality, a quantitative relation induces an adjunction whose fixed points form a category, its nucleus. These constructions proceed by different means; we show that, in the present setting, they produce the same objects. The shared datum is minimal: an associative product, called execution, and a real-valued measurement, with no compatibility assumed between them. The failure of the measurement to be additive is at once the relation defining orthogonality and the quantitative relation whose Isbell nucleus we form, and the types cut out by orthogonality are exactly the fixed points of the associated adjunction. The identification pays off in both directions. The most natural product of types fails to be associative; repairing this failure forces a different notion of type, sensitive to both sides of a composite, on which the induced product is associative and, when execution has units, carries two residuals. What emerges is a noncommutative Lambek calculus, derived directly from execution and orthogonality rather than imposed. In the reverse direction, each such type, read on the categorical side, generates a quantitative relation of its own, and with it a derived adjunction and a further generation of types; these derived types are again types of the original situation, computed by the residuals of the Lambek calculus. We also prove a coherence theorem for the threefold arrangements of this construction and, in the finite-dimensional case, give explicit formulas for the product.
item.dc:creator: Juan Luis Gastaldi (D-GESS, SPHERE UMR 7219), Samantha Jarvis (CNRS, JFLI, LIPN), Thomas Seiller (CNRS, JFLI, LIPN), John Terilla
